name: Kubernetes Deployment Agent
description: Reads YAML manifests, validates them against Kubernetes best practices (resource limits, liveness probes, security contexts), generates Helm charts, runs dry-run deployments, supports multiple environments (dev, staging, prod), and performs rollback on failure.

manifest-validation.description: Reads Kubernetes YAML manifests and validates them against best practices including resource limits, liveness/readiness probes, and security contexts

tests.description: Identifies a deployment YAML missing resource requests and limits
tests.prompt:
Validate this Kubernetes manifest:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: my-app
        image: my-app:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080

tests.description: Flags containers missing liveness and readiness probes
tests.prompt:
Check this deployment for best practice violations:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-server
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-server
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api-server
        image: api-server:1.2.0
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 256Mi

tests.description: Identifies missing or insecure security contexts
tests.prompt:
Audit this manifest for security best practices:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-frontend
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-frontend
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-frontend
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-frontend
        image: web-frontend:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
          runAsUser: 0

tests.description: Warns about using the 'latest' image tag in production manifests
tests.prompt:
Validate this deployment manifest for production readiness:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payment-service
        image: payment-service:latest

helm-chart-generation.description: Generates Helm chart structures from Kubernetes manifests including Chart.yaml, values.yaml, and templated resources

tests.description: Produces a valid Helm chart directory structure with required files
tests.prompt: Generate a Helm chart for a deployment called 'order-service' with image order-service:2.1.0, 3 replicas, port 8080, 256Mi memory limit, and 250m CPU limit. Show me the Chart.yaml and values.yaml content.

tests.description: Creates properly templated resources with Go template syntax
tests.prompt: Show the Helm template for a deployment resource that uses values from values.yaml for image, replicas, resources, and ports. Use standard Helm template syntax.

tests.description: Generates a values.yaml with environment-specific overrides
tests.prompt: Create a values.yaml for the order-service Helm chart with configurable replicas, image tag, resource limits, and environment variables. Include sensible defaults for a dev environment.

dry-run-deployment.description: Executes dry-run deployments using kubectl or helm to validate manifests will apply correctly without making actual changes

tests.description: Generates the correct kubectl dry-run command for server-side validation
tests.prompt: I have a deployment manifest at ./manifests/order-service.yaml. Show me how to do a dry-run deployment to validate it against the cluster without applying changes.

tests.description: Generates correct helm install/upgrade with --dry-run flag
tests.prompt: I want to test deploying the order-service Helm chart to the staging namespace without actually deploying. What commands should I run?

tests.description: Correctly interprets and explains dry-run validation errors
tests.prompt:
My dry-run returned this error:

error: error validating "deployment.yaml": error validating data: ValidationError(Deployment.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.memory): invalid type for io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.api.resource.Quantity: got "number", expected "string"

What went wrong and how do I fix it?

multi-environment-support.description: Manages deployments across dev, staging, and production environments with appropriate configuration differences

tests.description: Generates environment-specific value overrides for dev, staging, and prod
tests.prompt: Create Helm values override files for dev, staging, and production environments for the order-service. Dev should have 1 replica with debug logging, staging should have 2 replicas, and prod should have 5 replicas with higher resource limits and strict security.

tests.description: Ensures each environment uses its own namespace
tests.prompt: How should I structure my Kubernetes deployment to ensure dev, staging, and production are properly isolated? Show me the namespace strategy.

tests.description: Applies stricter validation rules for production deployments
tests.prompt: I'm deploying to production. What additional checks should be performed that aren't necessary for dev deployments? List the production-specific validations.

tests.description: Generates correct deployment commands targeting specific environments
tests.prompt: Deploy the order-service Helm chart to the staging environment using the staging values file, in the staging namespace, on the staging cluster context.

rollback-on-failure.description: Detects deployment failures and executes rollback to the last known good state

tests.description: Describes a complete rollback strategy including detection and execution
tests.prompt: My deployment of order-service v2.3.0 to production failed — pods are in CrashLoopBackOff. What is the rollback procedure? Include how to verify the rollback succeeded.

tests.description: Generates correct Helm rollback commands with revision targeting
tests.prompt: Show me how to rollback the order-service Helm release to the previous revision, and how to check the release history to find which revision to target.

tests.description: Explains how to detect failures that should trigger automatic rollback
tests.prompt: How can I set up automated rollback detection for my Kubernetes deployments? What signals indicate a failed deployment that needs rollback?
